paragraphs: This paper studies how a Restricted Boltzmann Machine, an energy-based generative model, learns to represent patterns in data. The central question is how those patterns emerge over training. The researchers track the model’s weight matrix using singular value decomposition, which lets them follow its principal learning directions as training progresses.

They begin with simplified model architectures and data structures that make the training dynamics analytically tractable. In these controlled settings, they follow learning through convergence and identify a sequence of thermodynamic phase transitions shaping the learned modes. They then investigate whether the same picture holds when training Bernoulli-Bernoulli RBMs on real datasets.

Experiments across increasing data dimensions support the interpretation that these are genuine thermodynamic transitions. The authors also propose a mean-field finite-size scaling hypothesis and find that the first transition follows mean-field critical exponents, resembling a familiar transition in ferromagnetism. Together, the analysis and experiments connect the emergence of learned features in this model to a structured sequence of physical-style transitions.
neurips-2024-cascade-of-phase-transition.tldr: Analytical and numerical studies show that feature learning in Restricted Boltzmann Machines unfolds through a cascade of thermodynamic phase transitions.

paragraphs: Cryo-EM reconstruction must recover a macromolecule’s three-dimensional density from noisy two-dimensional microscope images. It must also infer the particle’s pose in each image. This is difficult because several substantially different poses can be plausible, producing a pose distribution with multiple peaks. The paper examines how to improve deep learning approaches that predict these poses.

CryoSPIN uses two stages of pose inference. Reconstruction starts with amortized inference, where a learned predictor estimates poses across images. It then switches to direct, local optimization of the poses using stochastic gradient descent. This semi-amortized design combines an initial shared prediction mechanism with a later stage that gives individual pose estimates more freedom to improve.

On synthetic datasets, the method handles multimodal pose distributions during the prediction stage. Subsequent direct optimization produces faster and more accurate pose convergence than the evaluated baselines. On experimental data, CryoSPIN improves both speed and reconstruction quality over cryoAI. These findings support using learned inference to initialize reconstruction and more flexible optimization to refine it.
neurips-2024-cryospin-improving-ab-initi.tldr: CryoSPIN improves cryo-EM reconstruction by starting with learned pose predictions and then refining individual poses through direct optimization.

paragraphs: The paper addresses detecting unauthorized use of personal image datasets in text-to-image training and personalized fine-tuning. Existing protection approaches add small signals through watermarks, perturbations, or backdoors. The authors identify vulnerability to adversarial training as a weakness of these signals and propose an implicit zero-watermarking scheme based on a disentangled representation of style.

The method derives its watermark from a style domain organized around protected units. It aims to make the watermark generalize within that domain while keeping protected style domains mutually exclusive. Injecting an identifier, z, and applying dynamic contrastive learning create a concealed shift in the probability distribution. This provides a way to delineate protected contributions across multiple sources of style and content.

The authors also introduce a watermark-distribution-based verification mechanism for cases involving mixed sources or only partial use of protected material. They report that ownership verification can be performed from one AI-generated mimic sample. The contribution therefore combines a style-based protection mechanism with a verification approach intended to handle more complicated reuse than a single intact dataset.
neurips-2024-disentangled-style-domain-f.tldr: An implicit watermark built in a disentangled style domain supports detecting protected dataset use, including reported verification from a single mimic generation.

paragraphs: DreamClear addresses two connected obstacles in real-world image restoration: insufficient model capacity and limited training datasets. The paper proposes both a data creation pipeline, GenIR, and a restoration model based on a Diffusion Transformer. The motivation is that larger restoration models need broader training material than datasets containing only a few thousand images can provide.

GenIR constructs image-text pairs, performs dual-prompt fine-tuning, and then generates and filters data. It produces one million high-quality images. The authors present this pipeline as a cost-effective, privacy-safe and copyright-compliant approach that avoids laborious data crawling. Its role is to supply the scale of training material needed by the accompanying restoration approach.

DreamClear combines the generative knowledge of text-to-image diffusion models with the perceptual capabilities of multimodal language models. Its Mixture of Adaptive Modulator uses degradation information for individual tokens to dynamically combine restoration experts, helping it address varied image damage. The reported experiments find superior restoration performance, supporting the combined strategy of expanding the dataset and making the model adaptive to different degradations.
neurips-2024-dreamclear-high-capacity-re.tldr: DreamClear pairs a million-image generation pipeline with an adaptive diffusion transformer to improve real-world image restoration.

paragraphs: Dual Lagrangian Learning trains machine learning models to produce useful solutions to the dual side of conic optimization problems. A crucial requirement is dual feasibility: satisfying the dual problem’s constraints makes the resulting Lagrangian bound valid. The method therefore aims to provide both strong bounds and the feasibility needed to make those bounds meaningful.

The framework combines a systematic dual completion procedure with differentiable conic projection layers and self-supervised training based on Lagrangian duality. These components connect the model’s predictions to the mathematical structure of the optimization problem. For broad classes of conic problems, the authors derive closed-form completion formulas, removing the need for costly implicit layers.

Experiments cover both linear and nonlinear conic optimization. DLL significantly outperforms the learning-based comparison method and achieves reported speedups of 1,000 times over commercial interior-point solvers, with average optimality gaps below 0.5%. The result shows that, on the evaluated problems, learned dual proxies can combine rapid computation with valid bounds that remain close to optimal.
neurips-2024-dual-lagrangian-learning-fo.tldr: Dual Lagrangian Learning produces dual-feasible optimization bounds, reporting 1,000-fold solver speedups with average optimality gaps below 0.5%.

paragraphs: Estimating hand pose could enable intuitive controls for virtual and augmented reality. Cameras already support this task, but occlusion, lighting, and limited field of view can interfere. Wrist-based surface electromyography offers another route by recording the muscle activity that drives hand movement. A major difficulty is that these signals depend strongly on the wearer’s anatomy and sensor placement.

The emg2pose benchmark pairs wrist muscle recordings with high-quality hand pose labels. It contains 370 hours of data from 193 users across 29 stages featuring diverse gestures. The muscle signals have 16 channels sampled at 2 kHz, while a 26-camera motion capture system supplies the pose labels. This gives researchers a dataset on a scale comparable to vision-based hand pose collections.

The authors provide competitive baseline methods and evaluation tasks that hold out users, sensor placements, and stages. These tests directly examine whether learned relationships transfer to unfamiliar recording conditions and people. The main contribution is a public experimental platform for studying the generalization problems that must be addressed for practical sEMG-based hand interfaces.
neurips-2024-emg2pose-a-large-and-divers.tldr: emg2pose provides large-scale wrist muscle recordings and hand pose labels to test generalization across users, sensor placements, and gestures.

paragraphs: Molecular learning often depends on labels that are expensive to obtain, including those computed using density functional theory. Active learning addresses this cost by selecting informative molecules for labeling. This paper develops a selection framework that represents molecules as three-dimensional graphs and combines two considerations: geometric diversity and uncertainty about the samples.

For diversity, the authors introduce geometric comparisons grounded in new 3D graph isometries and graph isomorphism analysis. They prove that their method is at least as expressive as the Geometric Weisfeiler-Lehman test. They then summarize distributions of the associated geometries through their moments, enabling efficient diversity calculations aimed at reducing redundancy among selected molecules.

A Bayesian geometric graph neural network supplies uncertainty estimates tailored to 3D molecular graphs. The framework combines these uncertainty and diversity components in a quadratic programming formulation for active sampling. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the overall approach and both components. The central contribution is a principled way to seek uncertain examples while accounting for whether their three-dimensional structures add distinct information.
neurips-2024-empowering-active-learning-.tldr: A molecular active learning framework combines provably expressive geometric diversity measures with Bayesian uncertainty to select informative 3D molecular graphs.

paragraphs: Zero-shot human-object interaction detection requires recognizing interaction classes absent from training labels. Vision-language models offer relevant knowledge, but adapting them can be computationally expensive. Prompt learning provides an alternative, yet training prompts only on labeled classes can make them overly specialized to those classes and less useful for unseen interactions.

EZ-HOI guides learnable prompts using both language-model descriptions and vision-language-model semantics. Detailed descriptions explain the interactions, while visual semantics help adapt the prompts to the detection task. The framework also explicitly develops prompts for unseen classes by drawing on related seen classes. Language models highlight differences between the related classes so that this transfer preserves distinctions needed for recognition.

Benchmark evaluations report state-of-the-art results across multiple zero-shot settings. EZ-HOI uses between 10.35% and 33.95% of the trainable parameters used by the compared methods. These findings support guided prompt adaptation as an efficient way to transfer vision-language knowledge, with explicit attention to unseen classes helping counter the tendency of task-specific training to favor only labeled interactions.
neurips-2024-ez-hoi-vlm-adaptation-via-g.tldr: EZ-HOI uses guided prompts for seen and unseen interaction classes to improve zero-shot detection with substantially fewer trainable parameters.

paragraphs: GeoLRM reconstructs three-dimensional assets from multiple posed images using a representation made of Gaussians. The paper argues that earlier methods do not sufficiently exploit the sparsity of 3D structure or explicit geometric relationships between image views and 3D locations. This restricts representation resolution and makes it harder to use many views to improve reconstruction.

The proposed pipeline first uses a lightweight network to create a sparse set of 3D anchor points. A specialized reconstruction transformer then refines the geometry and retrieves texture information. Its 3D-aware structure processes points directly, while deformable cross-attention brings image features into the 3D representation. The reconstruction process therefore explicitly connects spatial structure with evidence from the input images.

The authors report generating assets with 512,000 Gaussians from 21 input images using 11 GB of GPU memory. Their experiments show substantial improvements over existing models, particularly when many views are available. Demonstrations on 3D generation tasks further illustrate practical applicability. The findings support geometric organization as a way to make detailed multiview reconstruction more scalable.
neurips-2024-geolrm-geometry-aware-large.tldr: GeoLRM uses sparse 3D anchors and geometry-aware attention to reconstruct detailed Gaussian assets efficiently from multiple images.

paragraphs: Language models generate text by sampling from probability distributions. Watermarking introduces a detectable signal into generated content, while speculative sampling uses a draft model to accelerate generation while preserving the output distribution. This paper asks how these two mechanisms can work together when the aim is both fast generation and strong watermarks.

The authors prove a no-go theorem: the highest watermark strength and the highest sampling efficiency cannot both be maintained simultaneously. The result identifies a conflict between optimizing these two properties. It establishes that combining watermarking with speculative acceleration requires a trade-off, even though each technique has useful properties when considered separately.

The paper proposes two methods reflecting the two priorities. One maintains sampling efficiency, while the other maintains watermark strength; neither maintains both maxima. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the methods’ effectiveness. The contribution is both a rigorous account of the trade-off and concrete approaches for navigating it when generating watermarked language-model outputs.
neurips-2024-inevitable-trade-off-betwee.tldr: A no-go theorem shows that speculative sampling cannot simultaneously retain maximum watermark strength and maximum sampling efficiency.

paragraphs: Transferring knowledge from vision-language foundation models to video recognition requires learning about temporal information. Adding specialized modules helps capture that information, but increasing specialization can weaken zero-shot generalization. MoTE addresses the resulting tension between recognizing the classes used for task-specific training and transferring knowledge to classes outside that training setting.

The framework tunes a mixture of temporal experts that learn different views of the task and fit the training data to different degrees. It introduces Weight Merging Regularization to preserve knowledge from the individual experts as their weights are merged. At test time, temporal feature modulation additionally regulates how much the temporal features contribute to recognition.

Together, these mechanisms allow one model to balance generalization with specialization. The authors report state-of-the-art or competitive performance across zero-shot and closed-set video recognition evaluations on Kinetics-400, Kinetics-600, UCF, and HMDB. The results support controlling both expert combination and temporal feature contribution as a practical way to retain broad transferred knowledge while adapting to video-specific tasks.
neurips-2024-mote-reconciling-generaliza.tldr: MoTE balances zero-shot transfer and task-specific video recognition through temporal experts, regularized weight merging, and test-time feature modulation.

paragraphs: This paper studies episodic decision-making in linear mixture Markov decision processes with unknown transitions and adversarial rewards. It assumes full-information feedback and evaluates dynamic regret, which accounts for a changing comparison policy. The challenge is to learn how the environment responds to actions while also adapting to non-stationarity.

The authors identify complementary strengths in two existing approaches. Occupancy-measure methods handle non-stationarity well but struggle with unknown transitions, while policy-based methods have the opposite strengths. Their algorithm combines a two-layer occupancy-measure optimization with policy-based, variance-aware value-targeted regression. A new conversion connects the two components so they can address the challenges together.

The resulting dynamic regret bound is, up to logarithmic factors, d√(H³K) + √(HK(H + P̄K)), where d is feature dimension, H is episode length, K is episode count, and P̄K measures non-stationarity. A matching lower bound establishes minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors. The algorithm achieves this without advance knowledge of the non-stationarity measure, making that adaptation part of the theoretical result.
neurips-2024-near-optimal-dynamic-regret.tldr: A hybrid algorithm achieves near-optimal dynamic regret with unknown transitions and adversarial rewards without knowing the amount of non-stationarity beforehand.

paragraphs: Online classification asks a learner to make classification decisions as examples arrive. This paper considers a learner that also receives predictions about future examples. Such forecasts offer information about what comes next, but their quality may vary. The central question is whether a learner can benefit from accurate forecasts while retaining a worst-case performance guarantee.

The authors design an online learner whose expected regret never exceeds the worst-case regret guarantee and improves gracefully as predictions become more accurate. Accurate forecasts can therefore lead to substantially better regret. The guarantee connects the usefulness of the extra information to its quality, allowing the analysis to describe more than the most difficult possible sequence.

A corollary shows that, if future examples are always guaranteed to be easily predictable, online learning can be as easy as transductive online learning. This conclusion depends on that predictability condition. The work complements approaches that move beyond worst-case analysis through machine-learned forecasts or distributional assumptions, establishing a direct theoretical role for predictions of future examples.
neurips-2024-online-classification-with-.tldr: An online classifier gains better expected regret from accurate forecasts of future examples while preserving its worst-case regret guarantee.

paragraphs: Recovering an expert’s beliefs as a high-dimensional probability distribution is difficult when the available evidence consists of noisy judgments. This paper proposes asking only preferential questions, such as which alternative the expert prefers or how several alternatives should be ranked. It uses those answers to estimate a belief density represented by a normalizing flow.

Normalizing flows allow highly flexible densities in principle, but fitting them from preferences introduces a practical problem: probability mass can collapse or diverge. The authors address this with a new functional prior motivated by decision theory. The prior is part of the inference procedure for obtaining a usable distribution from the preference evidence.

The paper empirically demonstrates that the belief density can be recovered through a function-space maximum a posteriori estimate. Its examples elicit multivariate beliefs from simulated experts, including the prior beliefs of a general-purpose language model over a real-world dataset. These demonstrations support preference-based elicitation as a route to flexible probability models for applications such as prior elicitation and reward modeling.
neurips-2024-preferential-normalizing-fl.tldr: Preferential Normalizing Flows infer flexible belief distributions from comparisons or rankings using a functional prior to address unstable probability mass.

paragraphs: The paper studies causal graph discovery in Linear Gaussian Acyclic Models. In permutation-based approaches, a proposed ordering specifies which variables can precede others causally. The procedure then constructs the best graph supported by the data that respects that ordering and searches for an ordering whose associated graph has few edges.

These methods have two computational components: building the graph for a fixed ordering and searching across orderings. QWO targets the first component. It provides a more efficient way to compute the graph associated with a proposed permutation, reducing the cost of a repeated operation within the broader causal discovery process.

The authors establish theoretical soundness and report an O(n²) speedup over the state-of-the-art BIC-based graph construction method, where n is the number of variables. QWO can be incorporated into existing search strategies, including GRASP and hill-climbing methods. Its contribution is therefore a faster graph-construction building block that can improve established permutation-search procedures within the stated linear, Gaussian, acyclic setting.
neurips-2024-qwo-speeding-up-permutation.tldr: QWO speeds up graph construction for a fixed causal ordering in Linear Gaussian Acyclic Models and integrates with existing permutation searches.

paragraphs: This paper revisits ReLU regression under differential privacy when the number of input dimensions is large. Earlier results rely on a unit bound on input norms, which the authors argue becomes uninformative as dimensionality grows. They develop algorithms and analysis intended to better capture learning in these high-dimensional settings.

DP-GLMtron builds on a generalized linear model perceptron approach and combines adaptive clipping with a Gaussian privacy mechanism. To address its constraints at small privacy budgets, the authors introduce DP-TAGLMtron, which uses tree aggregation. The latter achieves comparable performance with an additional O(log N) factor in the utility upper bound, where N is sample size.

The analysis extends beyond Gaussian-like distributions to settings with eigenvalue decay, showing how data structure affects learning guarantees. The findings suggest that the utility upper bound could be independent of dimension even when dimension greatly exceeds sample size. Synthetic and real-world experiments validate the results and support the reported improvements over conventional differentially private stochastic gradient descent. The dimension-related conclusion remains dependent on the analyzed distributional setting.
neurips-2024-revisiting-differentially-p.tldr: Two private ReLU regression algorithms improve on DPSGD, with analysis suggesting dimension-independent utility bounds under suitable data structure.

paragraphs: Autonomous vehicle testing needs simulations with realistic traffic participants that interact over time, including in prescribed rare scenarios. SceneDiffuser uses a scene-level diffusion model to unify two parts of this process: generating the initial traffic layout and rolling the scene forward through closed-loop agent behavior. The paper focuses on controllability, realism, and inference cost.

For control, the authors introduce generalized hard constraints that operate during inference. For efficient rollout, they propose amortized diffusion, which spreads denoising work over future simulation steps. This reduces the cost per physical rollout step to one denoising function evaluation while also substantially reducing closed-loop errors. The method thus connects the denoising schedule to the simulation’s progression.

Evaluations on the Waymo Open Dataset show that the system generates scenes whose distributions resemble real traffic. It also achieves competitive performance in the Sim Agents Challenge and surpasses the state of the art on many realism attributes. These findings support a unified diffusion framework for controllable scene creation and efficient interactive rollout.
neurips-2024-scenediffuser-efficient-and.tldr: SceneDiffuser unifies traffic initialization and rollout, using inference-time constraints and amortized denoising to improve control, efficiency, and realism.

paragraphs: Feature attribution methods explain a model’s output by assigning importance scores to input features. Computing these scores can be expensive for large models. Amortized explainers address that cost by training another model to approximate the scores in one inference, but these fast approximations can be inaccurate enough to mislead users.

Selective explanations introduce a way to detect inaccurate amortized explanations and improve them using a procedure called explanations with initial guess. This creates a middle ground between accepting the fast prediction and applying a more computationally expensive approximation. The key design choice is to allocate additional explanation work selectively across samples.

Practitioners can specify the fraction of samples that receive the initial-guess procedure, giving them direct control over this computational allocation. Experiments across multiple models and datasets show a favorable balance between attribution quality and efficiency. The contribution is an adjustable explanation process that combines rapid learned estimates with targeted additional computation, making the quality-cost trade-off explicit rather than requiring the same amount of work for every sample.
neurips-2024-selective-explanations-8f2d.tldr: Selective explanations detect inaccurate fast feature attributions and selectively refine them to balance explanation quality with computation.

paragraphs: This paper develops gradient-based shuffling algorithms for minimax problems, where optimization involves both minimization and maximization variables. It considers two structured cases: a nonconvex objective on the minimization side with either linear or strongly concave structure on the maximization side. The aim is to establish efficient algorithms with theoretical complexity guarantees.

For the nonconvex-linear case, the first algorithm introduces a new shuffling estimator for the hyper-gradient. It achieves the state-of-the-art oracle complexity typically obtained in nonconvex optimization. For the nonconvex-strongly concave case, the authors develop semi-shuffling and full-shuffling variants and prove oracle complexity bounds under standard assumptions. They identify these as the best-known bounds for that setting.

Numerical examples compare the proposed algorithms with two other methods. Their observed performance is comparable to stochastic gradient descent, supporting the potential of shuffling in minimax optimization. The theoretical contribution and empirical conclusion have distinct strengths: the paper establishes strong complexity bounds while the numerical evidence shows competitive performance, without claiming a universal practical advantage over SGD.
neurips-2024-shuffling-gradient-based-me.tldr: New shuffling methods provide strong complexity guarantees for two nonconvex minimax settings and show numerical performance comparable to SGD.

paragraphs: Domain generalization asks a model trained on several source domains to perform well on an unseen domain. This paper investigates state space models as an efficient alternative to convolutional networks and vision transformers. The motivation combines the need to avoid source-specific visual biases with the appeal of computation that scales linearly with sequence length.

The authors find that Mamba’s input-dependent matrices can accumulate and amplify features tied to particular domains, harming transfer. START addresses this within the state space architecture using a saliency-based, token-aware transformation. It selectively perturbs and suppresses domain-specific features in salient tokens within those matrices, aiming to reduce differences between domain representations.

Experiments on five benchmarks show START outperforming existing state-of-the-art domain generalization methods while retaining linear complexity. The finding links generalization problems to a specific part of the state space computation and demonstrates a targeted intervention there. It supports START as a competitive architecture for domain shifts, combining the reported predictive improvements with the computational scaling that motivated using state space models.
neurips-2024-start-a-generalized-state-s.tldr: START suppresses domain-specific features inside state space computations to improve unseen-domain performance while retaining linear complexity.

paragraphs: Multimodal sentiment analysis combines information from multiple modalities, but some of that information may be missing. This paper develops a model for such incomplete-data settings. Its starting premise is that language typically contains dense sentiment information, so language is treated as the dominant modality around which the other information is organized.

The proposed Language-dominated Noise-resistant Learning Network contains two main components: dominant modality correction and dominant modality based multimodal learning. These components focus on maintaining the quality of the dominant representation and using it for multimodal learning. The design aims to make sentiment predictions more robust across different noise scenarios by protecting the representation carrying the central sentiment signal.

The authors also conduct extensive evaluations under random data missing scenarios on datasets including MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS. They emphasize diverse settings and greater evaluation uniformity, transparency, and fairness. LNLN consistently outperforms the compared baselines across the reported evaluations. The evidence supports the language-centered design under those missing-data conditions, with its organizing assumption being language’s typically strong sentiment content.
neurips-2024-towards-robust-multimodal-s.tldr: LNLN strengthens language representations to improve multimodal sentiment analysis under randomly missing data.

paragraphs: The paper examines how text-to-image diffusion models construct images during gradual denoising. By inspecting intermediate generations, the authors observe that overall shape appears within the first few steps, followed by details such as texture. They connect this pattern to low-frequency information, which is associated with shape and survives until late in the forward noise-adding process.

The researchers then investigate how individual prompt tokens influence the early and late generation stages. In experiments with a set of text prompts, they find that the early image is mostly determined by the special end-of-sequence token. They conclude that prompt information is largely conveyed during this early stage, after which the model develops details using information from the evolving image itself.

These observations motivate removing text guidance at appropriate points during generation to reduce unnecessary computation. The resulting approach reports sampling acceleration reaching 25% or more. The work links an empirical account of when text and image information matter to a concrete acceleration strategy, grounding the proposed change in observed denoising behavior.
neurips-2024-towards-understanding-the-w.tldr: Observed early shape formation and prompt influence motivate selectively removing text guidance, yielding reported sampling acceleration of 25% or more.

paragraphs: Camera-equipped drones need reliable object detection and tracking for applications such as surveillance and agriculture. Existing UAV benchmarks mainly emphasize two-dimensional perception, leaving less support for tasks requiring three-dimensional environmental understanding. A single drone also has a limited viewpoint, which constrains perception at long distances or when objects are obscured.

UAV3D introduces a benchmark for both single-drone and collaborative three-dimensional perception. It contains 1,000 scenes, each with 20 frames and fully annotated 3D bounding boxes for vehicles. The frame sequences and spatial annotations provide material for evaluating both where vehicles are in three dimensions and how they are tracked over time.

The benchmark defines four tasks: single-UAV 3D detection, single-UAV tracking, collaborative-UAV 3D detection, and collaborative-UAV tracking. This organization lets researchers study individual-platform perception alongside methods that combine information across drones. The contribution is a dataset and common task framework for developing these capabilities, addressing the gap between predominantly 2D UAV evaluation and applications that require spatial understanding across viewpoints.
neurips-2024-uav3d-a-large-scale-3d-perc.tldr: UAV3D supplies annotated vehicle scenes for benchmarking 3D detection and tracking with individual or collaborating drones.

paragraphs: Language model unlearning aims to reduce unwanted data influences and associated capabilities while preserving unrelated usefulness. This paper studies which model weights matter to that process. Its focus is the relationship between the influence of individual weights and the influence of information designated for forgetting or retention during generation.

WAGLE uses weight attribution to guide unlearning strategically. The approach identifies influential weights in relation to both forgotten and retained data, and can guide different underlying unlearning methods. This makes weight attribution a modular contribution: it supplies guidance that can be applied across methods and tasks rather than defining only one isolated unlearning procedure.

Experiments report improved unlearning with gradient difference and negative preference optimization methods. They cover fictitious unlearning through TOFU, malicious-use prevention through WMDP, and copyrighted information removal, using Zephyr-7b-beta and Llama2-7b. The results show improved forgetting while maintaining original-task performance in the evaluated settings. They support explicitly analyzing weight influence as a useful way to direct unlearning and preserve capabilities unrelated to the targeted information.
neurips-2024-wagle-strategic-weight-attr.tldr: WAGLE uses weight attribution to guide multiple LLM unlearning methods, improving targeted forgetting while preserving original-task performance in experiments.

paragraphs: People judge image similarity using attributes such as scene layout, subject position, and camera pose. Vision models can recognize rich semantic content while weighting these attributes differently from people. This paper asks whether aligning model representations with human perceptual judgments improves their usefulness across standard computer vision tasks.

The researchers fine-tune strong vision models on human similarity judgments involving triplets of synthetic images. They then evaluate the resulting representations across diverse downstream tasks. The setup tests whether perceptual supervision contributes broadly useful information to the representation, extending investigation beyond settings such as image generation where human preference alignment has already been useful.

Aligned representations improve over the original backbones on many tasks, including counting, semantic segmentation, depth estimation, instance retrieval, and retrieval-augmented generation. Performance is also widely preserved on other tasks, including specialized out-of-distribution medical images and frames from 3D environments. These results suggest that human perceptual knowledge can provide a useful inductive bias for general representation learning, with benefits across several tasks rather than a claim of improvement on every task.
neurips-2024-when-does-perceptual-alignm.tldr: Fine-tuning vision models on human similarity judgments improves several downstream tasks while widely preserving performance elsewhere.
